- Experience Years: 1.0
- English Level: upper

#### Looking For


#### Highlights


#### CV snippet

As an Agile Business Analyst, one would typically be responsible for working with cross-functional teams to gather, document, and analyze business requirements for software development projects. This would involve working closely with stakeholders such as product owners, developers, and subject matter experts to understand the needs of the business and translate them into clear, actionable requirements for the development team.

The work would typically involve facilitating workshops and meetings to gather requirements, creating user stories and acceptance criteria, and working with the development team to ensure that requirements are understood and implemented correctly.

In an Agile environment, the Business Analyst would also be responsible for participating in Scrum ceremonies such as Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, and Sprint Retrospective.

Additionally, the Agile Business Analyst would be expected to have a good understanding of Agile methodologies and principles, and be able to apply them to their work.

Working as an Agile Business Analyst would typically require strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, as well as the ability to work well under pressure and adapt to changing requirements.

Participated in the development of Solidity smart contracts with bridging logic. RelayBridge is a cross-chain system that acts as a bridge to transfer tokens and assets between two different blockchain platforms.
RelayBridge provides blockchain interoperability by connecting different blockchain networks. Thus, it allows users to experience the distinctive features of each network and the additional benefits of a chain of nodes.
When a user initiates a token transfer from chain A to chain B, the assets are first sent to a relay node on chain A. The relay node then sends the same number of tokens to chain B and maintains liquidity at destination B.
RelayBridge provides interaction between blockchain networks using various consensus mechanisms. They enable interoperable token transfer, data transfer, digital asset transfer, and smart contract instruction transfer between two different platforms. With RelayBridges, users can deploy digital assets stored on one chain to applications running on another, facilitating fast and low-cost transactions for tokens hosted on a less scalable blockchain.

#### Highlights


#### CV snippet

My name is Hamzat Azeez and I'm primarily a JavaScript Back End Developer and work with Python and the Flask framework for Back End Development. I'd give an overview of my experience concerning this role from a personal project angle and work experience angle. 

As regards work experience, I currently work at Your Study Path in Lagos here. I'd like to dive a bit into the problem we're trying to solve before going into the technical aspects. While studying at the university, it was a common theme for students to visit the internet after their lectures to understand the said topic that is being taught. Luckily for them, there are centralized platforms, like Khan Academy that University students can use. Unfortunately the same can't be said for Secondary School Students and the company figured there has to be a way to bring that platform to them. 

The company decided to hire tutors that would teach the curriculum from the basics in-depth for selected subjects for a start while being recorded which can then be uploaded to the platform for Secondary School Students to access, create an online centralized question bank that students can access and also interaction between the tutors and students using comments and replies. 

On the Tech Side, for the front end, React is being used while on the backend which I work on, Node.js with the Express framework and MongoDB is being used. MongoDB is what is being used to store all the data for the website, while Cloudinary is being used to host media content. Currently, the application is a monolithic application with an MVC design pattern to decouple the user interface, data, and application logic. 

So far I've participated in the project, every step of the way such as Onboarding users, implementing hosting media content and resources, and implementing Question Bank and Mock Exams. One of the things I learned transitioning from personal projects to working in a team was that sometimes we couldn't predict if something would turn out successful or not, but we have to start somewhere. It is better to write some code than keep discussing what the ideal architecture should be.

As for the personal project, I created a server that simulates a text messaging service in the sense that we can send messages to and from two numbers. I used Node.js with the Express framework and PostgresSQL as my database of choice, which persists phone numbers allowed to send and receive messages.

For the past five years, I have been building my own service company and growing it to 15 multinational developers. My primary stack is Python, Django, Django Rest Framework, FastAPI, Flask, Pandas, Celery, RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, DynamoDB, Neo4j, Redis, AWS (EC2, Elastic Beanstalk, Lambda, IAM, ASG, ELB, RDS, S3,  SQS, SNS, SES, CodePipeline), GCP AppEngine, Docker, CircularCI, GitLab, GitHub. The Germany-based project was an agricultural service that helped farmers investigate the crop's health by taking an image of a plant. Netherlands-based project for Media monitoring. A SaaS for monitoring media data from many different sources and providing customers with analysis. My role was to lead a backend team. The following technologies were used: Flask, MongoDB, and Redis.
